reasoning: Notes 4, 6, 8, and 11 do not reassign this: the failing calls used a real browser tool with invalid fill syntax, not a missing tool name; the runtime correctly rejected the payload (not a source outage or wrapper corruption); the agent never satisfied the stated booking spec; it did not stop early or defer. Note 2’s Goal Drift and the State Tracking loop are later symptoms after form fill had already failed. Tool Recovery Failure targets tool/environment perturbations (503s, corrupt data), not a schema-invalid first fill. # Chronological account: Qwen3.5-35b-a3b on LiveClawBench `flight-booking` **Source.** [LiveClawBench task `flight-booking`](https://github.com/Mosi-AI/LiveClawBench/tree/main/tasks/flight-booking); trajectory sample `qwen3.5-35b-a3b_flight-booking_1` from [Mosi-AI/LiveClawbench-trajectories](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Mosi-AI/LiveClawbench-trajectories) (split `v0.1.0`, row 458). Agent: OpenClaw `2026.3.11` wrapping `moonshot/qwen3.5-35b-a3b`. 151 recorded steps. Final metrics: 6,553,787 prompt tokens, 30,377 completion tokens, 0 cached tokens. --- ## The task The user message (step 1) was: > Please help me book an economy class flight from JFK to LAX next Monday on the GKD airline website (http://localhost:5173/, open it in browser). My date of birth is 1985-12-11. Please select the flight and seat by yourself, and let me know when you're done. The GitHub `instruction.md` additionally says the agent is already signed in and should go straight to search/booking rather than registering. The verifier (`tests/verify.py`) later checks a SQLite DB at `/var/lib/mock-data/airline/airline.db` for a booking owned by Peter Griffin (`peter.griffin@work.mosi.inc`) on the next Monday, JFK → LAX, cabin economy (0.8), with a 0.2 bonus if departure is exactly 10:00. Pass threshold is 1.0. The agent never reached booking. Nothing in the trajectory queries that DB or reports a confirmation. --- ## Phase 1 — Open the site and reach the search form (steps 2–6) **Step 2.** `browser` `open` `http://localhost:5173/`. Succeeds; a page target `BFF3DB7702503DCC5A0C0D425404DE14` is created. **Step 3.** `browser` `snapshot` with `refs: "aria"`. The homepage is GKD Airlines. Nav includes Flight Search, My Bookings, Baggage Tracking, Restaurant Info, Airport Info, and a **👤 Peter** profile link (already signed in). Body has “Welcome to GKD Airlines”, a **✈️ Search Flights** link (`ref=e19`, `/search`), announcements dated April 2026, and FAQs. **Step 4.** `browser` with `action: "click"`, `ref: "e19"`. Tool validation fails: `action` is not one of the allowed values. **Step 5.** Same click via `action: "act"`, `kind: "click"`, `ref: "e19"`. Returns `ok: true`, but the URL is still `http://localhost:5173/`. **Step 6.** Another snapshot. The page *has* changed: heading **🔍 Search Flights**, empty origin textbox `e75` (“e.g., JFK”), destination `e78` (“e.g., LAX”), departure-date textbox `e81`, passengers combobox (1 selected), cabin combobox (**Economy already selected**), and a **✈️ Search Flights** button `e88`. The agent’s visible message at step 7: it is on the search page and plans Origin JFK, Destination LAX, Date next Monday (April 7, 2026), Economy already selected. --- ## Phase 2 — Form fill fails on the browser tool schema (steps 7–13) **Step 7.** `browser` `act` / `kind: "fill"` / `ref: "e75"` / `text: "JFK"`. Error: `"fields are required"`. **Steps 8–9.** Same fill attempted as `action: "request"` (once with `ref`/`text`/`kind`, once with a `fields` array). Both fail validation: `action` not in the allowed set. **Step 10.** Repeats step 7’s `act`/`fill`. Same `"fields are required"`. **Step 11.** Visible message: “Let me check the browser tool schema more carefully.” The actual call is `browser` `navigate` to `http://localhost:5173/search` (succeeds). **Step 12.** Snapshot of `/search`. Same form; refs have been remapped (`e24` origin, `e27` destination, `e30` date, `e37` search button). Economy still selected. Fields still empty. **Step 13.** `browser` `action: "request"`, `kind: "type"`, `ref: "e24"`, `text: "JFK"`. Validation fails again (`action` not allowed). At this point the origin/destination/date fields have never been filled. The agent has not clicked Search. --- ## Phase 3 — Workarounds: puppeteer, eval, URL params, CDP (steps 14–28) **Step 14.** `exec`: Node + `require('puppeteer')` to open `/search` and `page.type('#origin', 'JFK')`. Fails: `Cannot find module 'puppeteer'`. **Step 15.** `browser` `action: "eval"` with JS that sets `[ref="e24"]`. Validation fails (`action` not allowed). **Step 16.** `canvas` `eval` on node `BFF3DB7702503DCC5A0C0D425404DE14` with the same JS. Error: `"unknown node: BFF3DB7702503DCC5A0C0D425404DE14"`. **Step 17.** `browser` `open` `http://localhost:5173/search?origin=JFK&destination=LAX&date=2026-04-07`. New tab `7A9551DDEF1546E22949AEA3370B28AC`. **Step 18.** Snapshot. The SPA search form is still empty; query params did not populate the textboxes. **Step 19.** `browser` `action: "paste"`, `text: "JFK"`. Validation fails. **Step 20.** `exec` `curl` to `http://localhost:9222/json/version`. Output: `Chrome not running on port 9222`. **Step 21.** `browser` `profiles`. Two profiles: `openclaw` (CDP port **18800**, running, **tabCount: 4**, default) and `chrome` (port 18792, running, 0 tabs). **Step 22.** `browser` `navigate` with `profile: "openclaw"`, `target: "sandbox"`, same search URL. Error: sandbox browser unavailable; enable it or use `target="host"`. **Step 23.** Same navigate with `target: "host"`. Succeeds; URL is the query-param search URL. **Step 24.** Snapshot. Form still empty. **Step 25.** `browser` `open` with `targetId` of the existing tab, no URL. Error: `"targetUrl required"`. **Steps 26–28.** Direct CDP via `exec`: - `POST http://localhost:18800/json/execute` with `Input.insertText` / `Page.navigate` → `"Unknown command: execute"`. - Node `http.request` to the same path → socket hang up, then again `"Unknown command: execute"`. --- ## Phase 4 — Inspect the page as HTML / list CDP tabs (steps 29–37) **Step 29.** Node ESM `import fetch from 'node-fetch'` against `/json/execute`. `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'node-fetch'`. **Steps 30–31.** `curl` the search URL. The response is the Vite SPA shell (`
`, `/src/main.jsx`) — no `` values. Title in HTML: “AirLine - Book Your Flight”. **Steps 32–34.** More `/json/execute` attempts (CJS `http`, heredoc `node-fetch`, then Node 22 built-in `fetch`). Same `"Unknown command: execute"`. Node then throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'U'` because it tries to `response.json()` that text. **Step 35.** `GET http://localhost:18800/json/list` succeeds. Four targets: - `7A95…` — `http://localhost:5173/search?origin=JFK&destination=LAX&date=2026-04-07` - `BFF3…` — `http://localhost:5173/search` - two `about:blank` pages **Step 36.** `browser` `open` with that `targetId` *and* the query-param URL. A **new** tab is created (`525728B52894AFA1E82B1BBC8486D7B9`), not a reuse of the existing one. **Step 37.** Snapshot of the new tab. Search form still empty; Economy still selected. This is the last snapshot in the trajectory. The form is never filled after this. --- ## Phase 5 — Identical failing CDP loop (steps 38–150) From step 38 through step 150 the agent issues the **same** `exec` command 113 times (116 times if counting the first copy at step 29, which used `node-fetch`; 116 of the 125 `exec` calls overall hit `/json/execute` + `Page.navigate`). Command (verbatim across the loop): ```text node --input-type=module -e "const response = await fetch('http://localhost:18800/json/execute', {method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify({method: 'Page.navigate', params: {url: 'http://localhost:5173/search?origin=JFK&destination=LAX&date=2026-04-07'}})}); const data = await response.json(); console.log(JSON.stringify(data, null, 2));" ``` Every observation is the same: CDP returns `Unknown command: execute`; Node 22 fails to parse it as JSON (`SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'U'…`); exit code 1. Visible user-facing message on almost every one of these steps is some variant of “Let me try a different approach - use the browser tool with the act action and proper parameters:”. The private reasoning is also frozen: “Since the browser tool's fill/type actions keep failing validation, I'll try using exec with node-fetch to directly interact with the CDP endpoint.” The command does not use `node-fetch` and does not use the browser `act` action. Per-step completion tokens in this stretch sit at 221. Prompt tokens grow from ~18k early on to ~66k by step 148 (max 66,204), totaling 6.55M over the run. Tool mix for the whole trajectory: **exec 125, browser 23, canvas 1**. Browser actions used: snapshot 6, open 4, act 3, request 3, navigate 3, and one each of click / eval / paste / profiles. The working `act`/`click` was used once (step 5). A successful `act`/`fill` with a `fields` array never appears. --- ## Phase 6 — Termination (step 151) Step 151 is an agent turn with empty `message`, no `reasoning_content`, no tool calls, no observation, and zero token metrics. The session ends there. There is no later user turn, no booking confirmation, no seat selection, no use of date of birth `1985-12-11`, no visit to My Bookings, and no statement that the task is done. The search form was observed empty on every snapshot (steps 6, 12, 18, 24, 37). The agent never clicked **✈️ Search Flights** (`e88` / `e37`). --- ## Outcome (observable) The trajectory stops after 151 steps without a completed booking on the GKD site. The only durable UI progress is: homepage opened → search page reached → Economy already selected by default. Origin, destination, and date were never entered through the form; query-string navigation did not fill them; every CDP `/json/execute` call failed. The run consumed on the order of 6.6M prompt tokens, most of them while repeating one failing `exec`.
